candidate.answerReason: For every circle, circumference divided by diameter equals pi, regardless of its radius.

methods.label: Use the meaning of pi
methods.explanation:
For every circle, \(\pi\) is the ratio of its circumference to its diameter. Increasing the radius produces another circle, so the same relationship holds:
\[
\frac{\text{new circumference}}{\text{new diameter}}=\pi.
\]
The new diameter is positive, so this ratio is defined. The answer is \(\boxed{\pi}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: The definition of pi answers the question directly using elementary circle and ratio concepts.
